Hon’ble Alok Mahra, J.
Mr. Rishab Ranghar, learned counsel 
for the appellant.
2. Mr. V.D. Bisen, learned Addl. C.S.C. 
along with Mr. P.S. Bisht, learned Brief 
Holder for the State.
3. Learned counsel for the appellant 
would submit that in compliance with the 
order dated 19.06.2025 passed by the 
Coordinate Bench of this Court, service 
upon the respondents has been duly 
effected through publication in two national 
daily newspapers having wide circulation.
4. He would further submit that in 
compliance with the order dated 
09.10.2025, the appellant has filed an 
affidavit of service, indicating that the 
publication was duly made as directed.
5. The affidavit of service is taken on 
record. Perusal of the record reveals that
despite due publication of notice, none of 
the respondents have appeared or filed any 
objection.
6. Learned counsel for the appellant 
further submits that the appellant has filed 
a Miscellaneous Application (IA No. 2 of 
2025) supported by an affidavit, praying 
that the original documents filed in the 
record of the trial court be returned to the 
appellant, as the same are required in 
accordance with the provisions of Order XIII 
Rule 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908.
7. For the reasons stated in the 
application and supported by affidavit, the 
Miscellaneous Application (IA No. 2 of 2025)
is allowed. 8. The Registry is directed to return the 
original documents to the appellant, after 
retaining certified copies thereof on the 
record in terms of Order XIII Rule 9 CPC, 
and after making proper endorsement in 
the concerned register.
9. List this appeal for final hearing in due 
course.
(Alok Mahra, J.) 
 13.11.2025
Mamta

07 AO No.189 of 2025
Shivani Sharma and Another ........Appellants
v.
State of Uttarakhand ......Respondent
Hon’ble Ravindra Maithani, J.
Mr. Rishab Ranghar, Advocate for the 
appellants.
Mr. V.D. Bisen, Additional C.S.C. for 
the State.
Heard. 
The appellants sought permission to 
sell 50 per cent share of land in her name 
and in the name of her children Sameer 
Sharma and Sonali Sharma, under Sections 
7 and 8 of the Hindi Minority and 
Guardianship Act, 1956, and Sections 27 
and 29 of the Guardians and Wards Act, 
1890, on the ground that the son of the 
appellant Sameer Sharma is mentally 
retarded; he needs continuous caring; the 
property is big one. Therefore, the appellant
no.1, Shivani Sharma, wants to sell the 
property and purchase a small property so 
that her son Sameer Sharma can be looked 
after properly.
This application was rejected by the 
impugned judgment dated 19.04.2025, inter 
alia, on the ground that the appellant could 
not show as to how after the sale of the 
property, the interest of the son, Sameer
Sharma, would be protected.
In the application that was filed in the 
court below as well as in this appeal, Sonali 
Sharma, the another share holder of the 
property, is not a party. The property is joint 
and 50 per cent shares belongs to one 
Anupam Sharma. He is also not made the  party.
The Court posted a question to learned 
counsel for the appellants as to whether the 
brother in law of the appellant no.1, Shivani 
Sharma, and Sonali Sharma are agreeable to 
this sale, as proposed by the appellants? 
Learned counsel for the appellants seeks time 
to file affidavits of those two persons.
Let it be so filed within a week. 
List this matter on 03.07.2026, at 
02:15 p.m.
The appellant, Ms. Shivani Sharma, her 
daughter Sonali Sharma as well as Anupam 
Sharma shall join the proceedings on that 
date through video conferencing. 
 (Ravindra Maithani J.) 
19.06.2026
